baseline.method: Cumulative sampled allocations, including objects collected by minor/major GC, across the original bounded scenario. Sampling estimates are not continuous bounds.

postfix.method: Separate retained-only sampled allocations at the end of the fixed bounded scenario. Samples include retired engine storage not yet naturally collected; no heap snapshot/forced GC, no strong-retainer/leak conclusion. Different sampling mode, so these totals are not a before/after cumulative allocation comparison.

liveRun.method: Separate post-fix retained-only sampling profile. No forced GC; survivor samples also include retired engine storage awaiting natural collection and do not prove strong ownership. One minimal On cell compared with the retained four-cell baseline, 30 repeated previews for On, minimum 7 seconds each; no CLI rerun. Full retains original hook/status/trace/heartbeat/oracle costs; minimal uses 100ms main/phase-boundary renderer sampling and no retained plaintext oracle. OS private-commit monitor identical. Continuous shared allocator peak is separately reported. Sampling gives observed managed/native process costs, not a continuous JS/OS peak guarantee. Renderer component readings preserve backing/embedder attribution.

memory.method: GetProcessMemoryInfo for two owned PIDs. OS process-lifetime peak commit includes native/crypto/libuv and renderer external pages; incremental commit is not continuous logical allocation accounting. Private commit sampled at requested 2ms cadence; actual scheduler cadence unguaranteed.
